chapter: After the Army: school, race, politics
title: State Department tour with Billy Taylor and the circus animals
summary: Touring Europe with Billy Taylor and Grady Tate, Fuller played in circus tents, and his trombone upset the lions.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: We went tour with Dr. Billy Taylor. We took a group of musicians with the State Department over to Europe. All the venues didn’t have buildings, so we had to play with these tents with the circus. We had our own tent. You know? We got there while they’re setting up the tents and all the musicians practiced before the gig. There was these chairmen. It was true, every time I practiced my horns, all the lions, they sounded like the anvil chorus. They were (imitates a lion roaring), the polar bear went in here. Grady said, “Damn, Fuller! Whatever that sound is you got on this trombone, you’re upsetting all these animals!” Have you seen the picture, “The Wolf”?
You saw “Wolf” I’m sure you did. It was with Jack Nicholson. Ken Kimery: Oh yeah.

When he went around the horses and all that he goes, “Oh, shit!” (Laughs) Somebody said---But I gave them a (imitates himself playing) and the animals went wild. Grady had, on the bus, he had, “Yeah, every time Fuller picked up the trombone all the animals went nuts.” But, the point being is that music can reach the savage beast and whatever.
